title: What is G1 String Deduplication?
keyPoints: G1 GC can identify Strings with identical content and make them share the same byte[] array
Only works with G1 GC (default since Java 9)
Saves memory for applications with many duplicate Strings (logs, CSV data, web requests)
Different from intern(): dedup works on the char/byte array level, not the String object level

s1_definition.oneliner: G1 String Deduplication finds Strings with the same content and makes them share one byte[]. Saves memory without changing code. Enable with -XX:+UseStringDeduplication.
s1_definition.profdef:
How it works:

- **During GC,** G1 scans young-gen Strings.
- **If two Strings have the same content,** both point to one shared byte[] array. The duplicate array is freed.
- **The String objects remain separate** – only the internal array is shared.
- **No code changes needed.** Just a JVM flag.
s1_definition.analogy: Two bank branches have identical printed rate cards. Instead of each keeping their own copy, head office replaces both with one shared card. The branches still have their own display frames (String objects), but the printed content (byte[] array) is shared.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  String a = "SAV2001"  → byte[] {83,65,86,50,48,48,49}
  String b = "SAV2001"  → byte[] {83,65,86,50,48,48,49}  (separate copy)

  G1 Dedup:
    Detects a.value and b.value are identical
    Makes b.value point to a.value
    Frees b's original byte[]
    Memory saved: 1 byte[] per duplicate

  Enable: -XX:+UseStringDeduplication -XX:+UseG1GC
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
G1 String Deduplication automatically finds Strings with identical content and shares their internal byte[]. No code changes needed – just a JVM flag. Saves significant memory for applications with many duplicate Strings.

One sentence to remember: G1 dedup shares the byte[] array between identical Strings automatically – enable with -XX:+UseStringDeduplication.
